name: Prune Whip
author: Fannie Merritt Farmer (1896)
steps: Pick over and wash prunes, then soak several hours in cold water to cover; cook in same water until soft; remove stones and rub prunes through a strainer, add sugar, and cook five minutes; the mixture should be of the consistency of marmalade.
Beat whites of eggs until stiff, add prune mixture gradually when cold, and lemon juice.
Pile lightly on buttered pudding-dish, bake twenty minutes in slow oven.

culture.text: From The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896) by Fannie Merritt Farmer. It popularized level, standardized measurements (cups and spoons) in American home kitchens, and stayed one of the best-selling cookbooks in the United States for decades.
